signals.hidden_cause: Applied Materials is a semiconductor equipment supplier — it sits two steps upstream of AI end demand. The causal chain runs: AI compute demand → foundries and chipmakers plan fab expansions → wafer-fab-equipment demand improves → Applied Materials builds capacity ahead of anticipated orders. This is an expectation signal, not a confirmation: CapEx reflects management's assessment of customer capacity plans, not booked orders. The inference strengthens materially when accompanied by rising bookings, backlog growth, or revenue acceleration at downstream foundry customers.
alternative_explanations: AI semiconductor capacity expansion — demand propagates: AI models → GPUs → foundry capacity → equipment
Technology node transitions — gate-all-around (GAA), CoWoS advanced packaging, HBM manufacturing, advanced DRAM
CHIPS Act and government incentive programs — domestic fab investments subsidized by industrial policy
Overbuilding risk — semiconductor cycles show excess capacity after aggressive investment (2000, 2008, 2022)

signals.hidden_cause: Revenue acceleration at Arista Networks reflects hyperscalers and large AI infrastructure operators deploying high-performance Ethernet switching capacity to support AI training clusters. The causal chain is direct: AI training workloads generate dramatically more east-west traffic than traditional cloud → more Ethernet switching capacity required → Arista ships more systems → revenue recognized. Unlike many semiconductor signals where inventory and channel effects muddy interpretation, Arista sits close to actual network deployment — shipments correspond to infrastructure actively being brought online.
alternative_explanations: AI networking buildout — AI GPU clusters require dramatically more east-west traffic than traditional cloud, driving 400G/800G Ethernet switch deployments
Customer concentration — a few hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) drive most of Arista revenue; a few large deployments materially shift growth
Product mix upgrade to higher-ASP 400G/800G switches — revenue grows faster than unit shipments as customers upgrade bandwidth
Industry-wide networking cycle — general cloud infrastructure upturn benefits all networking equipment vendors, not AI-specific demand alone

A surge at this scale confirms AI data-center construction has moved from planning to active deployment: AI GPU cluster power density has risen to levels where traditional air cooling is insufficient, driving immediate demand for liquid cooling, precision power distribution, and high-density UPS systems. This is a physical deployment confirmation signal — one step closer to actual AI infrastructure activation than semiconductor CapEx or hyperscaler capex announcements.
alternative_explanations: AI data-center buildout — AI GPU clusters require 10–100x more power density than traditional racks, driving liquid cooling and precision power demand
Liquid cooling secular adoption — as rack power exceeds 30–60kW, air cooling reaches thermal limits and liquid cooling deployment accelerates
Backlog conversion timing — large data-center infrastructure projects shift revenue between quarters; growth may partly reflect prior backlog
Customer concentration — a few hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google) drive the majority of Vertiv's data center revenue

signals.observable: R&D intensity 29% of revenue with 31% YoY R&D growth
signals.hidden_cause: Meta's R&D investment reflects two distinct programs with different supply chain implications. The hardware-facing portion — AI training infrastructure, custom ASIC development (MTIA), and AR/VR hardware (Quest, smart glasses) — creates direct demand for AI compute silicon, networking chipsets, and optical components from real upstream suppliers. The software-facing portion — Llama model development, recommendation systems, and feed algorithms — generates no direct supplier orders. Management is betting that today's engineering investment will position Meta across AI platforms, wearables, and next-generation computing before revenue is visible.
alternative_explanations: Llama AI model development — training frontier LLMs requires massive GPU cluster investment and engineering talent
Reality Labs / AR-VR investment cycle — Quest headsets, Ray-Ban smart glasses, and future mixed-reality platform
AI infrastructure and training cluster buildout — scaling compute for recommendation systems, ads ranking, and content
Competitive response to OpenAI, Google (Gemini), and xAI (Grok) in foundational AI capabilities
